Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

new paragraph this morning rosie texted that mr bell had remembered the name of the ferry mechanic and wants to add it to his interview record i told her to send the spelling and the minute mark rather than changing the audio file she replied that she would check his consent sheet first and then write back i have not received the spelling yet so the log will say name to verify until she confirms it the scanner is packed with the foam in place the side entrance plan is written on the slip and the return deadline remains wednesday at five if the bus arrives after four twelve i will walk directly from market street and use the bell if the main doors are locked i still need to bring the case to the service desk and wait while staff check each item before the loan can be closed", "output": "Last Thursday I picked up the library scanner from the east branch for the oral history project. I had reserved it under my name, Lena Ortiz, and the desk worker checked my card and the equipment slip before she handed over the gray case. The reservation was for six days, with a return deadline of Wednesday at five in the afternoon. I had first written Tuesday in my notebook—no, Thursday; sorry, the pickup was Thursday and the due date was Wednesday the following week. The slip listed the scanner, the USB cable, the headset, and a small foam windscreen, but no wall charger because the library keeps those in a separate drawer.

The worker, named Priya, showed me the foam inside the case and pointed to a yellow tag tied to the handle. It said, “Keep the gain low in the meeting room because the ventilation fan can sound louder than a person speaking.” I asked whether I could use the scanner at the senior center as well as in the library, and she said yes, as long as it stayed in the county and came back by the printed deadline. She also explained that the battery usually lasts about four hours, but the screen gets dim when it is low. I brought my own charger and tested it at the counter. The battery showed three bars, and the headphone channel played clearly on both sides.

On Friday, I took the case to the North Harbor Senior Center, where my aunt Rosie had arranged short interviews with six former ferry workers. We booked the craft room from ten until one and taped a paper sign on the door so people would not walk through the recordings. The center manager, Calvin, asked me to keep the hallway clear because a meal cart comes through at eleven thirty. The room had two folding tables, a clock that ran seven minutes fast, and a radiator that clicked whenever it heated. I wrote those details in my notebook because they could explain noise in the audio later. The first interview began at ten twenty, after Mr. Bell finished a call to his daughter.

Before we started, Rosie read the consent paragraph aloud, and each person signed a separate sheet. Nobody asked to be recorded under a false name. Two people asked to use only their first names, and I noted that on the interview log. Mr. Bell wanted his full name attached to his memories but asked me not to include the street where he lives. He said, “I can talk about the old ferry all morning, but the new apartment block has nothing to do with it.” I checked that request with Rosie and wrote it beside his file number rather than on the public sign-out sheet. During his interview, the scanner captured his account of a winter crossing in 1982 and also caught the radiator clicking in the background.

At lunch, I checked the audio with the headset and found a soft scrape at the start of Rosie’s interview. I did not erase it because her chair had moved, and that was part of the original recording. I did reset the microphone stand and put a folded towel under its metal base for the remaining sessions. The windscreen stayed on even though Calvin offered to find a quieter room. He said the small room upstairs was free after one, but it had no ramp, and Mrs. Carter uses a walker. I told him we needed to remain in the accessible craft room. He said “beleza,” in the casual sense of “okay,” and helped move the second table closer to the wall.

The loan rules matter because if the scanner is returned late, the borrower owes a daily equipment fee and the next reservation may be canceled. The desk worker had told me that the county does not charge the fee when a branch closure prevents a return, but that does not cover a missed bus or a full parking lot. On Monday, I called the east branch to ask whether the box could be left in the book drop. The staff member said no because it contains electronics and has to be checked at the service desk. She said the branch would close at four on Wednesday for staff training, which was earlier than the five o’clock deadline on my slip. I asked if that meant there was an exception. She said she would check with the equipment coordinator and call me back rather than promise anything.

The coordinator called at two fifteen and said the return desk would stay open until five even though the reading room closed at four. She told me to use the side entrance and ring the bell if the main doors were locked. She also asked me not to leave the case with security because security staff cannot verify the inventory. I repeated the instructions to make sure I had them right, and she confirmed them. My cousin Erik had been planning to drive me, but his car was in the shop, so I arranged the number 42 bus instead. The timetable said the bus reached Market Street at four twelve, and the branch was a twelve-minute walk from that stop.

When I told Rosie about the schedule, she asked if I could wait until the end of the month to return the scanner because she wanted to record one more worker. I said I could only request an extension and could not assume it would be granted. She asked me to call that afternoon. I did, and the coordinator said another borrower had reserved the scanner starting Thursday, so an extra day was not available. She said I could ask about a different model but could not keep this one past Wednesday. I wrote down her exact answer and told Rosie that we would need to book another session after the next loan period instead of using the scanner without permission.

1. Before packing, I will compare the case contents with the slip and make sure the headset and cable are inside.
2. I will save a copy of each recording to the project drive and keep the original files unchanged.
3. I will place the signed consent sheets in Rosie’s locked folder and give the interview log to her in person.
4. I will return the scanner at the service desk by five on Wednesday. If the number 42 bus is delayed, I will call the east branch before four thirty and ask whether the return desk is still staffed. I will not use the book drop even if the side entrance is busy.

On Tuesday evening, I checked the battery again, and it still showed one bar, so I charged it at home. The green light came on after about two hours, and I left the case on a dry shelf away from the kitchen sink. I printed a fresh copy of the loan slip because the first one had coffee on the lower corner, and the due date was still readable but the branch phone number was not. I also packed a small notebook with the room notes, the three interview times, and Calvin’s reminder about the meal cart. On the return trip, I need to ask the desk worker to confirm that the windscreen is listed as part of the loan and to note the loose hinge on the case lid, which was loose when I picked it up. I have not asked for a replacement or reported damage because the hinge still closes and the tag is intact.

This morning, Rosie texted that Mr. Bell had remembered the name of the ferry mechanic and wants to add it to his interview record. I told her to send the spelling and the minute mark rather than changing the audio file. She replied that she would check his consent sheet first and then write back. I have not received the spelling yet, so the log will say “name to verify” until she confirms it. The scanner is packed with the foam in place, the side entrance plan is written on the slip, and the return deadline remains Wednesday at five. If the bus arrives after four twelve, I will walk directly from Market Street and use the bell if the main doors are locked. I still need to bring the case to the service desk and wait while staff check each item before the loan can be closed."}]
